text.p: The U.S. Defense Department on Friday described as "encouraging" an Iraqi statement that Iraq would stop firing at allied warplanes, but said the United States would watch the situation carefully.
"It certainly is an encouraging move toward reducing tensions in the Gulf if his (Iraq President Saddam Hussein's) words are followed by actions," Pentagon spokesman Ken Bacon told reporters.

Bacon declined to say whether the promising development might lead Washington to call off its plans for a possible attack against Iraq in retaliation for recent military challenges to allied planes patrolling no-fly zones.

But he indicated that for the time being the United States would continue its buildup of warplanes and ships in the Gulf region, saying: "We are moving forces to the Gulf necessary to protect our interests."

Bacon said no official word had been received in Washington of the conciliatory Iraqi move, but that news reports from Baghdad had been quickly passed on to Defence Secretary William Perry, Secretary of State Warren Christopher and National Security Adviser Anthony Lake. They were meeting to map out the next U.S. steps in the confrontation.

"It certainly will reduce the tensions if he (Saddam) stops shooting at our airplanes," Bacon said. At the White House, spokesman Mike McCurry said only that Washington would judge Iraq by its actions not its statements.
